{{Short description|Annual session of lectures}}
{{notability|date=March 2023}}

The '''Colloquium Lecture''' of the [[American Mathematical Society]] is a special annual session of lectures.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Parshall |first=Karen Hunger |author-link=Karen Parshall |date=2015-05-25 |title="Increasing the Utility of the Society": The Colloquium Lectures of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://journals.openedition.org/philosophiascientiae/1099 |journal=Philosophia Scientiæ. Travaux d'histoire et de philosophie des sciences |language=en |issue=19–2 |pages=153–169 |doi=10.4000/philosophiascientiae.1099 |issn=1281-2463 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== History ==
The origins of the Colloquium Lectures date back to the 1893 International Congress of Mathematics, held in connection with the [[Chicago World's Fair (1893)|Chicago World's Fair]], where the German mathematician [[Felix Klein]] gave the opening address.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1893 International Mathematical Congress - Chicago |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/ICM/ICM_Chicago_1893/ |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |language=en}}</ref> After the Congress, Klein was invited by one of its organiser, his former student [[Henry Seely White]], to deliver a two-week-long series of lectures at [[Northwestern University]] in [[Evanston, Illinois|Evanston]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=White |first=Henry S. |author-link=Henry Seely White |date=1894 |title=Klein's Evanston Lctures |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-new-york-mathematical-society/volume-3/issue-5/Kleins-Evanston-Lctures/bams/1183407831.full |journal=Bulletin of the New York Mathematical Society |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=119–122 |issn=2638-938X |via=[[Project Euclid]]}}</ref>

In February 1896, White proposed in a letter to [[Thomas Fiske]] to repeat the experience of the Evanston lectures, by organising a series of longer talks "for increasing the utility of the [[American Mathematical Society]]".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Henry White - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/White/ |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The two of them, together with [[E. H. Moore]], [[William Fogg Osgood|William Osgood]], [[Frank Nelson Cole|Frank Cole]], Alexander Ziwet, and [[Frank Morley]], wrote later an open letter to the AMS, asking the society to sponsor an annual week-long series of Colloquium lectures focussing on a specific mathematical area, in order to complement the traditional shorter talks.<ref name=":0" />

The first official Colloquium Lectures were held in September 1896, after the AMS Summer Meetings in [[Buffalo, New York]], and consisted of two independent series of lectures given by [[James Pierpont (mathematician)|James Pierpont]] and [[Maxime Bôcher]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Colloquium Lecturer |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/AMSCollLecturers/ |access-date=2023-03-25 |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |language=en}}</ref> A synopse of their lectures was published in the [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|Bulletin of the AMS]]; starting from the second Colloquium in 1898, the lectures have been published entirely in book form in the ''AMS Colloquium Publications'' series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colloquium Publications |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/content?PageName=coll |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}</ref>
